correctedFields.value: Strongest feature: The reply distinguishes personal existence from explanatory sufficiency, pressing the pro side to connect an ordinary executed teacher with the exalted, miracle-working Christ represented by the movement. Principal limitation: Its Superman and Clark Kent comparison leaves the causal criterion underdefined, while asking why crucifixion made anyone consequential does not engage the proposed intervening mechanism whereby followers interpreted him as resurrected. Live burden: The con case must comparatively evaluate resurrection belief and legendary development instead of requiring an unelaborated crucifixion itself to generate Christianity. Locked score: The strong band recognizes a proportionately qualified challenge to founder adequacy, tempered by incomplete engagement with the multistage explanation and an analogy that communicates intuition more effectively than evidentiary comparison.

Strongest feature: The move presents historical reconstruction as interpretive, question-guided, and revisable, using disagreement to caution against portraying Jesus portraiture as a straightforward extraction from neutral, comprehensive evidence. Principal limitation: A hermeneutical circle is not necessarily vicious when recalcitrant evidence corrects questions, while paradigm plurality alone establishes neither that existence judgments are unavailable nor that reconstructions have equivalent explanatory support. Live burden: The con side must specify where the historical-person framework resists correction and supply comparative criteria demonstrating that a mythic paradigm explains the evidence better. Locked score: The strong band recognizes thoughtful methodological relevance, appropriate modesty, and revisability, moderated by underdefined paradigm language and failure to transform interpretive underdetermination into a decisive objection concerning minimal existence.
